newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: CRICKET - Doull, Cork hold key to tests - Twose.
newsitem.headline: CRICKET - Doull, Cork hold key to tests - Twose.

text.p: WELLINGTON, Jan 8 - New Zealand's Simon Doull and England's Dominic Cork could hold the outcome of the England-New Zealand cricket test series in their bowling arms, according to Wellington captain and former English county professional Roger Twose.

Twose, who took up permanent residence in New Zealand two years ago after a highly successful career with champion county side Warwickshire, made his international debut last year for his adopted country.
He played Pakistan and Zimbabwe at home, played in the World Cup and toured the West Indies before opting out of the international game to play only for Wellington in this year's Shell series.
Most of the English team are known to Twose.

"The series will be very interesting. I think it will come down to the Simon Doull-Dominic Cork scenario. They are similar bowlers who are capable of bowling quick. They can swing the ball into and away from the batsmen," he told the New Zealand Press Association.
Twose said it would be unwise to read too much into the Zimbabwe leg of England's tour, in which England drew two tests and lost the one-day series 3-0.
There was not much between New Zealand and England in batting, he said.
"Zimbabwe will only have served to stir England up," he said.
Twose said he had no doubt that New Zealand should win the five-game one-day series, but the test series was too close to pick.

The latest international rankings show that New Zealand has moved off the last place it shared in the test rankings with Zimbabwe. It is still well below England, but England's rankings can be expected to drop next month after the Zimbabwe series.
On one-day rankings, New Zealand shares sixth place with Australia, one place ahead of the West Indies and one point behind India.
That table will also experience a shake-up next month after Zimbabwe's 3-0 win over England and the West Indies' improvements in Australia.
Meanwhile, the International Cricket Council has named the independent umpires for the series.
West Indian Steve Bucknor will stand in the first and second tests in Auckland and Wellington respectively while Australian Darrell Hair will stand in the third test in Christchurch.
Australian Peter Burge has already been named as the international match referee for the summer.
